title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 94 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 504–508 (Night 94, continuing directly from nights-93), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 94 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Dhāt al-Dawāhī finishes coaching her men in their story of the holy man imprisoned in a monastery, and has herself beaten and shut in a chest. In the Muslim camp, Ḍawʾ al-Makān and Sharrukān pledge Sharrukān's daughter Qaḍā Fakān to Ḍawʾ al-Makān's unborn son; the vizier Dandān urges them on with war verses, and the army marches for Constantinople to a paradise of a meadow. There the disguised 'merchants' arrive complaining of plunder, and take the two kings aside to tell them, weeping, the tale of the ascetic. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الرَّابِعَةُ وَالتِّسْعُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-rābiʿatu wa-al-tisʿūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the fourth-and-ninetieth,
sentences.i: And when it was the ninety-fourth night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الْعَجُوزَ ذَاتَ الدَّوَاهِي لَمَّا اتَّفَقَتْ مَعَ مَنْ مَعَهَا عَلَى هَذَا الْكَلَامِ قَالَتْ فَإِذَا أَلْقَى إِلَيْكُمْ سَمْعَهُ الْمَلِكُ شَرْكَانُ فَقُولُوا لَهُ فَلَمَّا سَمِعْنَا هَذَا الْكَلَامَ مِنْ تِلْكَ الصُّورَةِ عَلِمْنَا أَنَّ ذَلِكَ الْعَابِدَ مِنْ أَكَابِرِ الصَّالِحِينَ وَعِبَادِاللَّهِ الْمُخْلَصِينَ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-ʿajūza dhāta al-dawāhī lammā ittafaqat maʿa man maʿahā ʿalā hādhā al-kalāmi qālat fa-idhā alqā ilaykum samʿahu al-maliku sharrukānu fa-qūlū lahu fa-lammā samiʿnā hādhā al-kalāma min tilka al-ṣūrati ʿalimnā anna dhālika al-ʿābida min akābiri al-ṣāliḥīna wa-ʿibādi allāhi al-mukhlaṣīna
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī, when she had agreed with whoever was with her upon this speech, said: And when King Sharrukān casts to you his hearing, say to him: And when we heard this speech from that image, we knew that that worshipper was of the great-ones of the righteous and of the made-sincere servants-of-God;
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī had settled all this with her companions, she said, “When King Sharrukān gives you his ear, tell him: ‘When we heard these words from the picture, we knew that this holy man was one of the greatest of the righteous and of God's chosen servants.
sentences.n: The night opens by taking up the old woman's instructions where the last one broke off; everything from “When we heard” is the story she wants her men to tell. وعبادالله is printed as one word, wa-ʿibādi allāhi. al-mukhlaṣīn, “made sincere”, are those God has kept pure for Himself.

sentences.t: فَسَافَرْنَا مُدَّةَ ثَلٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ رَأَيْنَا ذَلِكَ الدَّيْرَ فَعَرَّجْنَا عَلَيْهِ وَمِلْنَا إِلَيْهِ وَأَقَمْنَا هُنَاكَ يَوْمًا فِى الْبَيْعِ وَالشِّرَاءِ عَلَى عَادَةِ التُّجَّارِ
sentences.tr: fa-sāfarnā muddata thalāthati ayyāmin thumma raʾaynā dhālika al-dayra fa-ʿarrajnā ʿalayhi wa-milnā ilayhi wa-aqamnā hunāka yawman fī al-bayʿi wa-al-shirāʾi ʿalā ʿādati al-tujjāri
sentences.l: So we travelled a space of three days, then we saw that monastery, and we turned-aside to it and inclined toward it, and stayed there a day in the selling and the buying, after the custom of the merchants;
sentences.i: So we travelled for three days, and then we sighted the monastery; we turned aside and made for it, and stayed there a day buying and selling, as merchants do.
sentences.n: ʿarraja ʿalā, to turn aside to a place on a journey. ثلٰثة is printed with the dagger alif.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَلَّى النَّهَارُ وَأَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ بِالِاعْتِكَارِ قَصَدْنَا تِلْكَ الصَّوْمَعَةَ الَّتِي فِيهَا السِّرْدَابُ فَسَمِعْنَاهُ بَعْدَ تِلَاوَةِ الْآيَاتِ يُنْشِدُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā wallā al-nahāru wa-aqbala al-laylu bi-al-iʿtikāri qaṣadnā tilka al-ṣawmaʿata allatī fīhā al-sirdābu fa-samiʿnāhu baʿda tilāwati al-āyāti yunshidu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: and when the day turned-away and the night came-on with the darkening, we made for that cell in which is the underground-vault, and we heard him, after the reciting of the verses, reciting these lines:
sentences.i: When the day was gone and the night came on in darkness, we made for the cell with the vault beneath it, and we heard him, after he had recited verses of the Qurʾān, chant these lines:’”
sentences.n: bi-al-iʿtikār, “with the darkening”: bi- gives the manner of the night's coming. Sajʿ: nahār/iʿtikār, āyāt/abyāt. The āyāt are verses of the Qurʾān, the abyāt lines of poetry: the holy man prays, then laments.

sentences.t:
كَبِدِيْ اُكَابِدُهُ وَصَدْرِي ضَيِّقُ * وَجَرَى بِقَلْبِي بَحْرُهُمْ مُغْرِقُ
اِنَّ لَمْ يَكُنْ فَرَجٌ فَمَوْتٌ عَاجِلٌ * اِنَّ الْحَمَامَ مِنَ الرَّزَايَا اَرْفَقُ
يَا بَرْقُ اِنْ جِئْتَ الدِّيَارَ وَاَهْلَهَا * وَعَلَا عَلَيْكَ مِنَ الْبَشَائِرِ رَوْنَقُ
كَيْفَ السَّبِيْلُ اِلَى اللِّقَاءِ وَبَيْنَنَا * تِلْكَ الْحُرُوْبُ وَبَابُ رَهْنٍ مُغْلَقُ
بَلِّغْ اَحِبَّتَنَا السَّلَامَ وَقُلْ لَهُمْ * اِنِّيْ بِدَيْرِ الرُّوْمِ قَاصِ مُوْثَقُ
sentences.tr:
kabidī ukābiduhu wa-ṣadrī ḍayyiqu * wa-jarā bi-qalbī baḥruhum mughriqu
inna lam yakun farajun fa-mawtun ʿājilun * inna al-ḥamāma mina al-razāyā arfaqu
yā barqu in jiʾta al-diyāra wa-ahlahā * wa-ʿalā ʿalayka mina al-bashāʾiri rawnaqu
kayfa al-sabīlu ilā al-liqāʾi wa-baynanā * tilka al-ḥurūbu wa-bābu rahnin mughlaqu
balligh aḥibbatanā al-salāma wa-qul lahum * innī bi-dayri al-rūmi qāṣi mūthaqu
sentences.l:
My liver, I suffer it, and my breast is strait, * and there has run in my heart their sea, drowning.
If there is not a relief, then a death swift: * truly the death, of the calamities, is the gentler.
O lightning, if you come to the abodes and their people, * and there rose upon you of the good-tidings a lustre —
how is the way to the meeting, when between us * are those wars, and a gate of pledge shut?
Convey to our beloved-ones the greeting, and say to them: * I am in the monastery of the Rūm, far, bound.
sentences.i:
My liver I endure, and my breast is tight, * and through my heart their drowning sea has run.
If no relief comes, then let death come swiftly: * of all misfortunes death is the kindest.
O lightning, if you reach the dwellings and their people, * and the gleam of good tidings shines on you —
how can we meet, when there stand between us * these wars, and a hostage's gate locked fast?
Bring our loved ones greeting, and tell them: * I am far away, a prisoner in the monastery of the Rūm.
sentences.n: Verse, as printed with its own pointing. Two of the printed vowels are not what the sense wants and are kept: the second line opens اِنَّ, “truly”, where the sense is اِنْ, “if”; and الْحَمَامَ is pointed ḥamām, “doves”, where the sense is ḥimām, “death”. “Their sea” is the sea of longing for his people. قَاصِ stands for qāṣin, “far”. “My liver”: in Arabic verse the liver, not the heart, is the seat of the deepest grief.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ إِذَا وَصَلْتُمْ بِي إِلَى عَسْكَرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَصِرْتُ عِنْدَهُمْ كَيْفَ أُدَبِّرُ حِيلَةً فِي خَدِيعَتِهِمْ وَقَتْلِهِمْ عَنْ آخِرِهِمْ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat idhā waṣaltum bī ilā ʿaskari al-muslimīna wa-ṣirtu ʿindahum kayfa udabbiru ḥīlatan fī khadīʿatihim wa-qatlihim ʿan ākhirihim
sentences.l: Then she said: When you have arrived with me at the army of the Muslims and I have become with them — how I will contrive a stratagem in the deceiving of them and the killing of them to the last of them!
sentences.i: Then she said, “Once you have brought me to the Muslim army and I am among them, you will see how I contrive a trick to deceive them and kill them to the last man.”
sentences.n: The sentence breaks off at kayfa, “how”: “— and then, how I will …!” waṣala bi-, “arrive with”, is “bring”. ʿan ākhirihim, “to the last of them”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ النَّصَارَى كَلَامَ الْعَجُوزِ قَبَّلُوا يَدَيْهَا وَوَضَعُوهَا فِى الصُّنْدُوقِ بَعْدَ أَنْ ضَرَبُوهَا أَشَدَّ الضَّرَبَاتِ الْمُوجِعَاتِ تَعْظِيمًا لَهَا لِأَنَّهُمْ يَرَوْنَ طَاعَتَهَا مِنَ الْوَاجِبَاتِ ثُمَّ قَصَدُوا بِهَا عَسْكَرَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ كَمَا ذَكَرْنَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-naṣārā kalāma al-ʿajūzi qabbalū yadayhā wa-waḍaʿūhā fī al-ṣundūqi baʿda an ḍarabūhā ashadda al-ḍarabāti al-mūjiʿāti taʿẓīman lahā li-annahum yarawna ṭāʿatahā mina al-wājibāti thumma qaṣadū bihā ʿaskara al-muslimīna kamā dhakarnā
sentences.l: And when the Christians heard the speech of the old woman, they kissed her two hands and put her in the chest, after they had beaten her the hardest of the blows, the painful-ones, in honouring of her, because they see obedience to her as of the duties; then they made with her for the army of the Muslims, as we have mentioned.
sentences.i: When the Christians heard the old woman's words they kissed her hands and laid her in the chest, after beating her with the cruellest, most painful blows — out of reverence for her, since they held obedience to her a sacred duty. Then they set off with her for the Muslim camp, as we have told.
sentences.n: taʿẓīman lahā, “in honour of her”: they beat her because she ordered it, and to obey her was their duty. Sajʿ: mūjiʿāt/wājibāt.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ هَذِةِ اللَّعِينَةِ ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي وَمَنْ مَعَهَا
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amri hādhihi al-laʿīnati dhāti al-dawāhī wa-man maʿahā
sentences.l: This is what there was of the affair of this accursed-one, Dhāt al-Dawāhī, and whoever was with her.
sentences.i: So much for the accursed Dhāt al-Dawāhī and her companions.
sentences.n: هذة, with tāʾ marbūṭa, is the edition's spelling of هذه, hādhihi.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ عَسْكَرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَإِنَّهُمْ لَمَّا نَصَرَهُمُ اللَّهُ عَلَى أَعْدَائِهِمْ وَغَنِمُوا مَا كَانَ فِى الْمَرَاكِبِ مِنَ الْأَمْوَالِ وَالذَّخَائِرِ قَعَدُوا يَتَحَدَّثُونَ مَعَ بَعْضِهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri ʿaskari al-muslimīna fa-innahum lammā naṣarahumu allāhu ʿalā aʿdāʾihim wa-ghanimū mā kāna fī al-marākibi mina al-amwāli wa-al-dhakhāʾiri qaʿadū yataḥaddathūna maʿa baʿḍihim
sentences.l: And as for what there was of the affair of the army of the Muslims: they, when God had given them victory over their enemies and they had plundered what was in the ships of the wealth and the treasures, sat talking with one another.
sentences.i: As for the Muslim army: when God had given them the victory over their enemies and they had taken as spoil the riches and stores in the ships, they sat down to talk together.
sentences.n: maʿa baʿḍihim, “with some of them”, is the everyday reciprocal, “with one another”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ لِأَخِيهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ نَصَرَنَا بِسَبَبِ عَدْلِنَا وَانْقِيَادِنَا لِبَعْضِنَا فَكُنْ يَا شَرْكَانُ مُمْتَثِلًا لِأَمْرِي فِي طَاعَةِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ لِأَنِّي نَوَيْتُ أَنْ أَقْتُلَ عَشَرَةَ مُلُوكٍ عِوَضًا عَنْ أَبِي وَأَذْبَحَ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفًا مِنَ الرُّومِ وَأَدْخُلَ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ḍawʾu al-makāni li-akhīhi inna allāha naṣaranā bi-sababi ʿadlinā wa-inqiyādinā li-baʿḍinā fa-kun yā sharrukānu mumtathilan li-amrī fī ṭāʿati allāhi ʿazza wa-jalla li-annī nawaytu an aqtula ʿasharata mulūkin ʿiwaḍan ʿan abī wa-adhbaḥa khamsīna alfan mina al-rūmi wa-adkhula al-qusṭanṭīniyyata
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to his brother: God has given us victory because of our justice and our submitting to one another; so be, O Sharrukān, obedient to my command in the obedience of God, mighty and glorious, for I have intended that I kill ten kings in exchange for my father, and slaughter fifty thousand of the Rūm, and enter Constantinople.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to his brother, “God has given us the victory because we were just and gave way to one another. So, Sharrukān, do as I command in obeying God, mighty and glorious is He; for I have resolved to kill ten kings to pay for my father, to slaughter fifty thousand of the Rūm, and to enter Constantinople.”
sentences.n: ʿiwaḍan ʿan abī, “in exchange for my father”: their father, King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, was murdered through Dhāt al-Dawāhī's plotting, and this is the blood-price. li- in li-amrī: “to my command”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَخُوهُ شَرْكَانُ رُوحِي فِدَاؤُكَ مِنَ الرَّدَى وَلَابُدَّلِي مِنَ الْجِهَادِ وَلَوْأُ قِيمُ فِي بِلَادِهِمْ سِنِينَ عَدِيدَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu akhūhu sharrukānu rūḥī fidāʾuka mina al-radā wa-lā budda lī mina al-jihādi wa-law uqīmu fī bilādihim sinīna ʿadīdatan
sentences.l: And his brother Sharrukān said to him: My soul is your ransom from the destruction, and there is no escape for me from the holy-war, even if I stay in their lands years many.
sentences.i: His brother Sharrukān answered, “My life be your ransom from harm! I must fight this holy war, even if it keeps me in their lands for years on end.
sentences.n: The print sets ولو اقيم as ولوا قيم, carrying the alif over to the first word, and ولا بد لي solid as ولابدلي; the spacing is kept as printed. rūḥī fidāʾuka, “my soul your ransom”, is a formula of devotion.

sentences.t: لَكِنْ يَا أَخِي لِي فِي دِمَشْقَ ابْنَةٌ وَاسْمُهَا قَضَى فَكَانَ وَقَلْبِي مُتَعَلِّقٌ بِحُبِّهَا وَهِيَ مِنْ غَرَائِبِ الزَّمَانِ وَسَيَكُونُ لَهَا شَأْنٌ
sentences.tr: lākin yā akhī lī fī dimashqa ibnatun wa-ismuhā qaḍā fakāna wa-qalbī mutaʿalliqun bi-ḥubbihā wa-hiya min gharāʾibi al-zamāni wa-sa-yakūnu lahā shaʾnun
sentences.l: But, O my brother, I have in Damascus a daughter, and her name is Qaḍā Fakān, and my heart is hung on the love of her, and she is of the wonders of the time, and there will be to her a standing.
sentences.i: But, brother, I have a daughter in Damascus named Qaḍā Fakān. My heart clings to her; she is one of the marvels of the age, and she will make her mark.”
sentences.n: Qaḍā Fakān, “what was decreed came to be”, is the daughter's name, a phrase kept as the print gives it. sa-yakūnu lahā shaʾn, “she will have a standing”: she will be someone. شان, without its hamza, is the edition's spelling.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَأَنَا الْآخَرُ تَرَكْتُ جَارِيَتِي وَهِيَ حُبْلَى عَلَى مِيلَادٍ وَمَا أَدْرِي مَايَرْزُقُنِي اللَّهُ بِهِ فَيَا أَخِي عَاهِدْنِي إِنْ رَزَقَنِي اللَّهُ وَلَدًا ذَكَرًا تَسْمَحُ لِي بِابْنَتِكَ قَضَى فَكَانَ أَنْ تَكُونَ لِوَلَدِي وَتُعْطِينِي الْمَوَاثِيقَ وَالْأَيْمَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-anā al-ākharu taraktu jāriyatī wa-hiya ḥublā ʿalā mīlādin wa-mā adrī mā yarzuqunī allāhu bihi fa-yā akhī ʿāhidnī in razaqanī allāhu waladan dhakaran tasmaḥu lī bi-ibnatika qaḍā fakāna an takūna li-waladī wa-tuʿṭīnī al-mawāthīqa wa-al-aymāna
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: And I, the other, left my slave-girl and she pregnant, near to a birth, and I do not know what God will provide me with; so, O my brother, covenant with me: if God provides me a child male, you grant me your daughter Qaḍā Fakān, that she be for my son, and you give me the compacts and the oaths.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān said, “I too left my slave-girl behind with child, near her time, and I do not know what God will grant me. So, brother, give me your word: if God grants me a son, you will grant your daughter Qaḍā Fakān to be his, and pledge me your bond and your oath on it.”
sentences.n: anā al-ākhar, “I the other”, is colloquial for “I too”. مايرزقني is printed as one word, mā yarzuqunī; rizq is God's provision, here a child. samaḥa li bi-, “grant me”: bi- marks the thing granted.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ شَرْكَانُ حُبًّا وَكَرَامَةً وَمَدَّ يَدَةُ إِلَى أَخِيهِ وَقَالَ إِنْ جَاءَكَ وَلَدًا أُعْطِيَنَّهُ ابْنَتِي قَضَى فَكَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla sharrukānu ḥubban wa-karāmatan wa-madda yadahu ilā akhīhi wa-qāla in jāʾaka waladan uʿṭiyannahu ibnatī qaḍā fakāna
sentences.l: And Sharrukān said: Lovingly and honourably; and he stretched his hand to his brother and said: If there comes to you a son, I shall surely give him my daughter Qaḍā Fakān.
sentences.i: “With all my heart and gladly,” said Sharrukān, and he held out his hand to his brother and said, “If a son is born to you, I will give him my daughter Qaḍā Fakān.”
sentences.n: ḥubban wa-karāmatan, “out of love and honour”, is the formula of a willing yes. waladan, with the accusative ending where Classical needs the nominative walad, is a Middle Arabic habit. uʿṭiyannahu is the emphatic (energetic) form, “I shall surely give him”. يدة, with tāʾ marbūṭa, is the edition's spelling of يده, yadahu.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ بِذَلِكَ وَصَارَ يُهَنِّي بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضًا بِالنَّصْرِ عَلَى الْأَعْدَاءِ وَهَنَّى الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ شَرْكَانَ وَأَخَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa bi-dhālika wa-ṣāra yuhannī baʿḍuhum baʿḍan bi-al-naṣri ʿalā al-aʿdāʾi wa-hannā al-wazīru dandānu sharrukāna wa-akhāhu
sentences.l: And he rejoiced at that, and there began, some of them, to congratulate others on the victory over the enemies; and the vizier Dandān congratulated Sharrukān and his brother
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān rejoiced at this, and they all began to congratulate one another on the victory over the enemy. The vizier Dandān congratulated Sharrukān and his brother
sentences.n: yuhannī and hannā are the spoken forms of yuhanniʾu and hannaʾa, “congratulate”, with the hamza dropped. ṣāra with an imperfect: “began to”. bi- in bi-al-naṣri: “on” the victory.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُمَا اعْلَمَا أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكَانِ أَنَّ اللَّهَ نَصَرَنَا حَيْثُ وَهَبْنَا أَنْفُسَنَا لِلَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَهَجَرْنَا الْأَهْلَ وَالْأَوْطَانَ وَالرَّأْيُ عِنْدِي أَنْ نَرْحَلَ وَرَاءَهُمْ وَنُحَاصِرَهُمْ وَنُقَاتِلَهُمْ لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ أَنْ يُبَلِّغَنَا مُرَادَنَا وَنَسْتَأْصِلَ أَعْدَائَنَا
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahumā iʿlamā ayyuhā al-malikāni anna allāha naṣaranā ḥaythu wahabnā anfusanā li-allāhi ʿazza wa-jalla wa-hajarnā al-ahla wa-al-awṭāna wa-al-raʾyu ʿindī an narḥala warāʾahum wa-nuḥāṣirahum wa-nuqātilahum laʿalla allāha an yuballighanā murādanā wa-nastaʾṣila aʿdāʾanā
sentences.l: and said to them: Know, O you two kings, that God gave us victory inasmuch as we gave our souls to God, mighty and glorious, and forsook the family and the homelands; and the opinion with me is that we march behind them and besiege them and fight them; perhaps God will bring us to our desire, and we uproot our enemies.
sentences.i: and said to them, “Know, my kings, that God gave us the victory because we gave ourselves to God, mighty and glorious is He, and left our families and our homelands behind. My counsel is that we march after them, besiege them and fight them; perhaps God will grant us our wish and we shall tear our enemies out by the root.
sentences.n: ḥaythu, “where”, does duty here for “since, because”. laʿalla … an, “perhaps … that”, mixes two constructions, a post-Classical habit. اعدائنا, with ئ, is the edition's spelling of aʿdāʾanā.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ شِئْتُمْ فَانْزِلُوا فِي هَذِةِ الْمَرَاكِبِ وَسِيرُوا فِى الْبَحْرِ وَنَحْنُ نَسِيرُ فِى الْبَرِّ وَنَصْبِرُ عَلَى الْقِتَالِ وَالطَّعْنِ فِى النِّزَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-in shiʾtum fa-inzilū fī hādhihi al-marākibi wa-sīrū fī al-baḥri wa-naḥnu nasīru fī al-barri wa-naṣbiru ʿalā al-qitāli wa-al-ṭaʿni fī al-nizāli
sentences.l: And if you wish, then go-down into these ships and travel on the sea, and we will travel on the land and be-steadfast upon the fighting and the thrusting in the combat.
sentences.i: If you wish, embark in these ships and go by sea, while we go by land and stand firm through the battle and the spear-thrusts of single combat.”
sentences.n: nazala fī, “go down into”, is to board a ship. Sajʿ: qitāl/nizāl.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ مَا زَالَ يُحَرِّضُهُمْ عَلَى الْقِتَالِ وَأَنْشَدَ قَوْلَ مَنْ قَالَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-wazīra dandāna mā zāla yuḥarriḍuhum ʿalā al-qitāli wa-anshada qawla man qāla
sentences.l: Then the vizier Dandān did not cease urging them on to the fighting, and he recited the saying of him who said:
sentences.i: And the vizier Dandān kept urging them on to battle, and recited the words of the poet:

sentences.t:
اَطْيَبُ الطَّيِّبَاتِ قَتْلُ ٱلْاَعَادِي * وَاحْتِمَالِي عَلَى ظُهُوْرِ ٱلْجِيَادِ
وَرَسُوْلُ يَأْتِي بِوَعْدِ حَبِيْبٍ * وَحَبِيْبٌ يَأْتِي بِلَا مِيْعَادِ
sentences.tr:
aṭyabu al-ṭayyibāti qatlu al-aʿādī * wa-iḥtimālī ʿalā ẓuhūri al-jiyādi
wa-rasūlu yaʾtī bi-waʿdi ḥabībin * wa-ḥabībun yaʾtī bi-lā mīʿādi
sentences.l:
The sweetest of the sweet-things is the killing of the enemies, * and my being-carried upon the backs of the steeds,
and a messenger who comes with a promise of a beloved, * and a beloved who comes without an appointment.
sentences.i:
Sweetest of sweet things is to kill one's enemies, * and to be borne on the backs of thoroughbreds,
and a messenger who comes with a lover's promise, * and a lover who comes with no appointment made.
sentences.n: The print has يَأْنِي, a misprint for يَأْتِي (yaʾtī, “comes”), corrected here; the rest of the verse is as printed. وَرَسُوْلُ is printed without its nunation (rasūlun). bi-lā mīʿād, “with no appointment”: bi-lā is “without”.

sentences.t: وَقَوْلَ الْآخَرِ
sentences.tr: wa-qawla al-ākhari
sentences.l: and the saying of the other:
sentences.i: and the words of another:
sentences.n: qawla is still the object of anshada, “he recited”.

sentences.t:
وَاِنْ عُمِرْتُ جَعَلْتُ الْحَرْبَ وَالِدَةً * وَالسَّمْهَرِيَّ اَخًا وَالْمَشْرَفِيَّ اَبَا
بِكُلِّ اَشْعَثَ يَلْقَى الْمَوْتَ مُبْتَسِمًا * حَتَّى كَاَنَّ لَهُ فِي قَتْلِهِ اَرَبَا
sentences.tr:
wa-in ʿumirtu jaʿaltu al-ḥarba wālidatan * wa-al-samhariyya akhan wa-al-mashrafiyya abā
bi-kulli ashʿatha yalqā al-mawta mubtasiman * ḥattā ka-anna lahu fī qatlihi araba
sentences.l:
And if I am given-long-life, I will make the war a mother, * and the Samharī-spear a brother, and the Mashrafī-sword a father,
with every dishevelled-one who meets the death smiling, * until as if there were to him in his being-killed a desire.
sentences.i:
If I am granted long life, I shall make war my mother, * the Samharī spear my brother and the Mashrafī sword my father,
with every wild-haired warrior who meets death smiling, * as though to be slain were what he longed for.
sentences.n: Verse, as printed with its own pointing. The Samharī is a famous kind of spear, called after Samhar, a spear-maker of legend; the Mashrafī a sword from the Mashārif, the uplands of Syria. ashʿath, “dishevelled, dusty-haired”, is the hardened fighter with no time for grooming. abā, for the accusative aban, is lengthened for the rhyme. bi-kulli: “with”, in the company of.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ مِنْ شِعْرِةِ قٰلَ سُبْحَانَ مَنْ أَيَّدَنَا بِنَصْرِةِ الْعَزِيزِ وَظَفَّرَنَا بِغَنِيمَةِ الْفِضَّةِ وَالْإِبْرِيزِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha al-wazīru dandānu min shiʿrihi qāla subḥāna man ayyadanā bi-naṣrihi al-ʿazīzi wa-ẓaffaranā bi-ghanīmati al-fiḍḍati wa-al-ibrīzi
sentences.l: And when the vizier Dandān had finished from his verse, he said: Glory to Him who strengthened us with His victory the mighty, and made-us-win the booty of the silver and the pure-gold.
sentences.i: When the vizier Dandān had finished his verses, he said, “Glory to Him who upheld us with His mighty victory and gave us the spoil of silver and pure gold!”
sentences.n: قل is the edition's short spelling of قال, qāla; شعرة and بنصرة, with tāʾ marbūṭa, are its spellings of شعره and بنصره. bi- in bi-naṣrihi: “with, by means of” His victory; ẓaffara bi-, “make (someone) win (something)”. Sajʿ: ʿazīz/ibrīz.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَمَرَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ الْعَسْكَرَ بِالرَّحِيلِ فَسَافَرُوا طَالِبِينَ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةَ وَجَدُّوا فِي سَيْرِهِمْ حَتَّى أَشْرَفُوا عَلَى مَرْجٍ فَسِيحٍ وَفِيهِ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ مَلِيحٍ مَا بَيْنَ وُحُوشٍ تَمْرَحُ وَغِزْلَانٍ تَسْنَحُ
sentences.tr: thumma amara ḍawʾu al-makāni al-ʿaskara bi-al-raḥīli fa-sāfarū ṭālibīna al-qusṭanṭīniyyata wa-jaddū fī sayrihim ḥattā ashrafū ʿalā marjin fasīḥin wa-fīhi kullu shayʾin malīḥin mā bayna wuḥūshin tamraḥu wa-ghizlānin tasnaḥu
sentences.l: Then Ḍawʾ al-Makān commanded the army to the departure, and they travelled seeking Constantinople, and were earnest in their going until they looked-down upon a meadow wide, and in it every thing comely, between wild-beasts frolicking and gazelles crossing.
sentences.i: Then Ḍawʾ al-Makān ordered the army to march, and they set out for Constantinople. They pressed on hard until they came out above a broad meadow full of every lovely thing, wild beasts at play and gazelles darting across their path.
sentences.n: amara bi-, “command”: bi- marks the thing commanded. sanaḥa is said of game that crosses the traveller's path. Sajʿ: fasīḥ/malīḥ, tamraḥ/tasnaḥ.

sentences.t: وَكَانُوا قَدْ قَطَعُوا مَفَاوِزَ كَثِيرَةً وَانْقَطَعَ عَنْهُمُ الْمَاءُ سِتَّةَ أَيَّامٍ
sentences.tr: wa-kānū qad qaṭaʿū mafāwiza kathīratan wa-inqaṭaʿa ʿanhumu al-māʾu sittata ayyāmin
sentences.l: And they had crossed deserts many, and the water had been cut off from them six days.
sentences.i: They had crossed many deserts, and for six days they had been without water.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَشْرَفُوا عَلَى ذَلِكَ الْمَرْجِ نَظَرُوا تِلْكَ الْعُيُونَ النَّابِعَةَ وَالْأَثْمَارَ الْيَانِعَةَ وَتِلْكَ الْأَرْضَ كَأَنَّهَا جَنَّةٌ أَخَذَتْ زُخْرُفَهَا وَازَّيَّنَتْ وَسَكِرَتْ أَغْصَانُهَا مِنْ رَحِيقِ الطَّلِّ فَتَمَايَلَتْ وَجَمَعَتْ بَيْنَ عُذُوبَةِ التَّسْنِيمِ وَاعْتِلَالِ النَّسِيمِ فَتُدْهِشُ الْعَقْلَ وَالنَّاظِرَ كَمَا قَالَ الشَّاعِرُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ashrafū ʿalā dhālika al-marji naẓarū tilka al-ʿuyūna al-nābiʿata wa-al-athmāra al-yāniʿata wa-tilka al-arḍa ka-annahā jannatun akhadhat zukhrufahā wa-izzayyanat wa-sakirat aghṣānuhā min raḥīqi al-ṭalli fa-tamāyalat wa-jamaʿat bayna ʿudhūbati al-tasnīmi wa-iʿtilāli al-nasīmi fa-tudhishu al-ʿaqla wa-al-nāẓira kamā qāla al-shāʿiru
sentences.l: And when they looked-down upon that meadow, they beheld those springs, the welling-ones, and the fruits, the ripe-ones, and that land as if it were a garden that had taken its adornment and decked-itself, and its branches had grown-drunk from the nectar of the dew, so they swayed; and it joined between the sweetness of the Tasnīm and the languor of the breeze, so it amazes the mind and the beholder, as the poet said:
sentences.i: When they came out above the meadow they saw its welling springs and ripe fruits, a land like a garden of Paradise that had put on its finery and adorned itself; its branches, drunk on the wine of the dew, swayed to and fro, and it joined the sweetness of Tasnīm to the soft languor of the breeze, so that it dazzled mind and eye — as the poet says:
sentences.n: “Taken its finery and adorned itself” echoes Qurʾān 10:24, of the earth in full bloom. Tasnīm is a spring of Paradise (Qurʾān 83:27). naẓara with a direct object, without ilā: “beheld”. Sajʿ: nābiʿa/yāniʿa, tasnīm/nasīm.

sentences.t:
اُنْظُرْ اِلَى الرَّوْضِ النَّضِيْرِ كَاَنَّمَا * نُشِرَتْ عَلَيْهِ مَلَاءَةٌ خَضْرَاءُ
اِنْ مَا سَنَحْتَ بِلَحْظِ عَيْنِكَ لَاتَرَى * اِلَّا غَدِيْراً جَالَ فِيْهِ الْمَاءُ
وَتَرَى بِنَفْسِكَ عِزَّةً فِيْ دَوْحِهِ * اِذْفَوْقَ رَأْسِكَ حَيْثُ سِرْتَ لِوَاءُ
sentences.tr:
unẓur ilā al-rawḍi al-naḍīri ka-annamā * nushirat ʿalayhi malāʾatun khaḍrāʾu
in mā sanaḥta bi-laḥẓi ʿaynika lā tarā * illā ghadīran jāla fīhi al-māʾu
wa-tarā bi-nafsika ʿizzatan fī dawḥihi * idh fawqa raʾsika ḥaythu sirta liwāʾu
sentences.n: Verse, as printed with its own pointing. لَاتَرَى and اِذْفَوْقَ are printed as one word each, lā tarā and idh fawqa. The banner is the canopy of branches overhead.

sentences.t: وَكَمَا قَالَ الْآخَرُ
sentences.tr: wa-ka-mā qāla al-ākharu
sentences.l: And as the other said:
sentences.i: And as another says:

sentences.t:
اَلنَّهْرُ خَدٌّ بِالشُّعَاعِ مُوَرَّدٌ * قَدْ دَبَّ فِيْهِ عِذَارُ ظِلِّ الْبَانِ
وَالْمَاءُ فِيْ سُوْقِ الْغُصُوْنِ خَلَاخِلٌ * مِنْ فِضَّةٍ وَالزَّهْرُ كَالتِّيْجَانِ
sentences.tr:
al-nahru khaddun bi-al-shuʿāʿi muwarradun * qad dabba fīhi ʿidhāru ẓilli al-bāni
wa-al-māʾu fī sūqi al-ghuṣūni khalākhilun * min fiḍḍatin wa-al-zahru ka-al-tījāni
sentences.l:
The river is a cheek, by the sunbeam rosy, * there has crept on it the down of the shade of the bān-tree;
and the water on the shanks of the branches is anklets * of silver, and the blossom like the crowns.
sentences.i:
The river is a cheek flushed rose by the sunlight, * where the ban-trees' shadow creeps like a young man's first beard;
the water is silver anklets on the legs of the boughs, * and the blossoms are like crowns.
sentences.n: Verse, as printed with its own pointing. ʿidhār is the first down on a youth's cheek, a stock image of beauty in Arabic verse: here the dark shade of the trees on the bright water. sūq, plural of sāq, “shank”, is also a tree's trunk. bi- in bi-al-shuʿāʿi: “by” the sunbeam.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ إِلَى ذَلِكَ الْمَرْجِ الَّذِي الْتَفَّتْ أَشْجَارُهُ وَزَهَتْ أَزْهَارُهُ وَتَرَنَّمَتْ أَطْيَارُهُ نَادَى أَخَاهُ شَرْكَانَ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا أَخِي إِنَّ دِمَشْقًا مَا فِيهَا مِثْلُ هَذَا الْمَكَانِ فَلَا نَرْحَلُ مِنْهُ إِلَّا بَعْدَ ثَلٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍ حَتَّى نَأْخُذَ لَنَا رَاحَةً لِأَجْلِ أَنْ تَنْشَطَ عَسَاكِرُ الْإِسْلَامِ وَتَقْوَى نُفُوسُهُمْ عَلَى لِقَاءِ الْكَفَرَةِ اللِّئَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓara ḍawʾu al-makāni ilā dhālika al-marji alladhī iltaffat ashjāruhu wa-zahat azhāruhu wa-tarannamat aṭyāruhu nādā akhāhu sharrukāna wa-qāla lahu yā akhī inna dimashqan mā fīhā mithlu hādhā al-makāni fa-lā narḥalu minhu illā baʿda thalāthati ayyāmin ḥattā naʾkhudha lanā rāḥatan li-ajli an tanshaṭa ʿasākiru al-islāmi wa-taqwā nufūsuhum ʿalā liqāʾi al-kafarati al-liʾāmi
sentences.l: And when Ḍawʾ al-Makān looked at that meadow whose trees were intertwined and whose flowers were radiant and whose birds trilled, he called his brother Sharrukān and said to him: O my brother, Damascus — there is not in it the like of this place; so we will not depart from it except after three days, that we may take for ourselves a rest, for the sake that the armies of Islam may grow-lively and their souls be strong for the meeting of the unbelievers, the base-ones.
sentences.i: When Ḍawʾ al-Makān looked out over that meadow, its trees thick-woven, its flowers in bloom, its birds singing, he called to his brother Sharrukān and said, “Brother, there is no place like this in all Damascus. We will not leave it for three days, so that we can rest, and the armies of Islam can recover their spirits and gather strength to meet the base unbelievers.”
sentences.n: دمشقا, with the accusative ending -an, declines Dimashq fully; Classical treats it as a diptote, Dimashqa. Sajʿ: ashjāruhu/azhāruhu/aṭyāruhu, islām/liʾām.

sentences.t: فَأَقَامُوا فِيهِ فَبَيْنَمَا هُمْ كَذَلِكَ إِذْ سَمِعُوا أَصْوَاتًا مِنْ بَعِيدٍ
sentences.tr: fa-aqāmū fīhi fa-baynamā hum ka-dhālika idh samiʿū aṣwātan min baʿīdin
sentences.l: So they stayed in it; and while they were thus, lo, they heard voices from afar.
sentences.i: So they encamped there; and as they rested, they heard voices in the distance.

sentences.t: فَسَأَلَ عَنْهُمْ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ فَقِيلَ لَهُ إِنَّهَا قَافِلَةُ تُجَّارٍ مِنْ بِلَادِ الشَّامِ كَانُوا نَازِلِينَ فِي هَذَا الْمَكَانِ لِلرَّاحَةِ لَعَلَّ الْعَسَاكِرَ صَادَمُوهُمْ وَرُبَّمَا أَخَذُوا شَيْأً مِنْ بَضَائِعِهِمُ الَّتِي مَعَهُمْ حَيْثُ كَانُوا فِى بِلَادِ الْكُفَّارِ
sentences.tr: fa-saʾala ʿanhum ḍawʾu al-makāni fa-qīla lahu innahā qāfilatu tujjārin min bilādi al-shāmi kānū nāzilīna fī hādhā al-makāni li-al-rāḥati laʿalla al-ʿasākira ṣādamūhum wa-rubbamā akhadhū shayʾan min baḍāʾiʿihimu allatī maʿahum ḥaythu kānū fī bilādi al-kuffāri
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān asked about them, and it was said to him: It is a caravan of merchants from the lands of Syria; they were halting in this place for the rest; perhaps the troops collided-with them, and perhaps they took a thing of their goods which were with them, since they were in the lands of the unbelievers.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān asked who they were, and was told, “A caravan of merchants from Syria who had stopped in this place to rest. The troops may have run into them and taken some of their goods, since they were in the unbelievers' country.”
sentences.n: ḥaythu, “where”, again does duty for “since”: merchants found in enemy country could be taken for fair game.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ سَاعَةٍ جَاءَ التُّجَّارُ وَهُمْ صَارِخُونَ يَسْتَغِيثُونَ بِالْمَلِكِ فَلَمَّا رَأَى ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ ذَلِكَ أَمَرَ بِإِحْضَارِهِمْ فَحَضَرُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda sāʿatin jāʾa al-tujjāru wa-hum ṣārikhūna yastaghīthūna bi-al-maliki fa-lammā raʾā ḍawʾu al-makāni dhālika amara bi-iḥḍārihim fa-ḥaḍarū bayna yadayhi
sentences.l: And after an hour the merchants came, and they crying-out, calling-for-help on the king; and when Ḍawʾ al-Makān saw that, he commanded the bringing of them, and they came-present between his two hands
sentences.i: A little later the merchants came, crying out and appealing to the king for help. When Ḍawʾ al-Makān saw this he had them brought, and they stood before him
sentences.n: istaghātha bi-, “call on someone for help”: bi- marks the one appealed to. bayna yadayhi, “between his two hands”, is “before him, in his presence”.

sentences.t: وَقَالُوا أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ إِنَّا كُنَّا فِي بِلَادِ الْكُفَّارِ وَلَمْ يَنْهَبُوا مِنَّا شَيْأً فَكَيْفَ تَنْهَبُ أَمْوَالَنَا إِخْوَانُنَا الْمُسْلِمُونَ وَنَحْنُ فِي بِلَادِهِمْ فَإِنَّنَا لَمَّا رَأَيْنَا عَسَاكِرَكُمْ أَقْبَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ فَأَخَذُوا مَا كَانَ مَعَنَا وَقَدْ أَخْبَرْنَاكَ بِمَا حَصَلَ لَنَا
sentences.tr: wa-qālū ayyuhā al-maliku innā kunnā fī bilādi al-kuffāri wa-lam yanhabū minnā shayʾan fa-kayfa tanhabu amwālanā ikhwānunā al-muslimūna wa-naḥnu fī bilādihim fa-innanā lammā raʾaynā ʿasākirakum aqbalnā ʿalayhim fa-akhadhū mā kāna maʿanā wa-qad akhbarnāka bi-mā ḥaṣala lanā
sentences.l: and they said: O king, we were in the lands of the unbelievers and they did not plunder from us a thing; so how do our brothers the Muslims plunder our wealth, and we in their lands? For we, when we saw your armies, came-forward to them, and they took what was with us; and we have told you what befell us.
sentences.i: and said, “O king, we were in the unbelievers' country and they never robbed us of a thing. How then can our own brothers, the Muslims, plunder our goods when we are in their territory? When we saw your armies we came towards them, and they took everything we had. Now we have told you what has happened to us.”
sentences.n: akhbara bi-, “inform of”: bi- marks the news. tanhabu, singular before its plural subject ikhwānunā, as Classical allows when the verb comes first.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَخْرَجُوا لَهُ كِتَابَ مَلِكِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ فَأَخَذَةُ شَرْكَانُ وَقَرَأَ
sentences.tr: thumma akhrajū lahu kitāba maliki al-qusṭanṭīniyyati fa-akhadhahu sharrukānu wa-qaraʾa
sentences.l: Then they brought-out to him the letter of the king of Constantinople, and Sharrukān took it and read;
sentences.i: Then they produced for him a letter from the king of Constantinople. Sharrukān took it and read it,
sentences.n: فاخذة, with tāʾ marbūṭa, is the edition's spelling of فاخذه, fa-akhadhahu, “and he took it”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُمْ سَوْفَ نَرُدُّ عَلَيْكُمْ مَا أُخِذَ مِنْكُمْ وَلَكِنْ كَانَ الْوَاجِبُ أَنْ لَاتَحْمِلُوا تِجَارَةً إِلَى بِلَادِ الْكُفَّارِ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla lahum sawfa naruddu ʿalaykum mā ukhidha minkum wa-lākin kāna al-wājibu an lā taḥmilū tijāratan ilā bilādi al-kuffāri
sentences.l: then he said to them: We shall return to you what was taken from you; but it was the duty that you not carry merchandise to the lands of the unbelievers.
sentences.i: then said to them, “We will give you back what was taken from you. But you ought never to have carried goods into the unbelievers' country.”
sentences.n: لاتحملوا is printed as one word, lā taḥmilū.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا يَامَوْلَانَا إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَيَّرَنَا إِلَى بِلَادِهِمْ لِنَظْفَرَ بِمَالَمْ يَظْفَرْ بِهِ أَحَدٌ مِنَ الْغُزَاةِ وَلَا أَنْتُمْ فِي غَزَوَاتِكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū yā mawlānā inna allāha sayyaranā ilā bilādihim li-naẓfara bi-mā lam yaẓfar bihi aḥadun mina al-ghuzāti wa-lā antum fī ghazawātikum
sentences.l: And they said: O our lord, God made-us-travel to their lands that we might win what no one of the raiders has won, nor you in your raids.
sentences.i: “Our lord,” they said, “God sent us into their country so that we might win a prize such as no raider has ever won, not even you in all your campaigns.”
sentences.n: يامولانا and بمالم are printed as one word each. ẓafira bi-, “win, lay hands on”: bi- marks the prize.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمْ شَرْكَانُ وَمَا الَّذِي ظَفِرْتُمْ بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahum sharrukānu wa-mā alladhī ẓafirtum bihi
sentences.l: And Sharrukān said to them: And what is that which you have won?
sentences.i: “And what is it you have won?” Sharrukān asked them.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا مَا نَذْكُرُ ذَلِكَ إِلَّا فِى الْخَلْوَةِ لِأَنَّ هَذَا الْأَمْرَ إِذَا شَاعَ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ رُبَّمَا اطَّلَعَ عَلَيْهِ أَحَدٌ فَيَكُونُ ذَلِكَ سَبَبًا لِهَلَاكِنَا وَهَلَاكِ كُلِّ مَنْ يَتَوَجَّهُ إِلَى بِلَادِ الرُّومِ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū mā nadhkuru dhālika illā fī al-khalwati li-anna hādhā al-amra idhā shāʿa bayna al-nāsi rubbamā iṭṭalaʿa ʿalayhi aḥadun fa-yakūnu dhālika sababan li-halākinā wa-halāki kulli man yatawajjahu ilā bilādi al-rūmi mina al-muslimīna
sentences.l: And they said: We will not mention that except in the privacy, because this matter, if it spreads among the people, perhaps someone will get-knowledge of it, and that will be a cause for our destruction and the destruction of every one who heads to the lands of the Rūm of the Muslims.
sentences.i: “We will speak of it only in private,” they said, “for if this got about, someone might come to hear of it, and that would be the death of us and of every Muslim who travels to the land of the Rūm.”

sentences.t: وَكَانُوا قَدْ خَبَؤُا الصُّنْدُوقَ الَّذِي فِيهِ اللَّعِينَةُ ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي فَأَخَذَهُمْ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَأَخُوهُ وَاخْتَلَيَا بِهِمْ فَشَرَحُوا لَهُمَا حَدِيثَ الزَّاهِدِ وَصَارُوا يَبْكُونَ حَتَّى أَبْكَوْهُمَا
sentences.tr: wa-kānū qad khabaʾū al-ṣundūqa alladhī fīhi al-laʿīnatu dhātu al-dawāhī fa-akhadhahum ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-akhūhu wa-ikhtalayā bihim fa-sharaḥū lahumā ḥadītha al-zāhidi wa-ṣārū yabkūna ḥattā abkawhumā
sentences.l: And they had hidden the chest in which was the accursed-one, Dhāt al-Dawāhī. And Ḍawʾ al-Makān and his brother took them and were-alone with them, and they laid-out to the two of them the story of the ascetic, and began weeping until they made the two of them weep.
sentences.i: They had hidden away the chest that held the accursed Dhāt al-Dawāhī. Ḍawʾ al-Makān and his brother took them aside in private, and the merchants told them the story of the ascetic, weeping as they told it, until the two kings wept too.
sentences.n: ikhtalā bi-, “be alone with”: bi- marks the company. The “ascetic” is the old woman herself, in her disguise.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The closing formula, as in every night.
